title: Second reviewer on P-L4-004: across the twelve zodiac centres I find the same single freestanding Voynich label, beside the upper star on f70v2; every other centre holds only the emblem and a word in the other script
statement: A second pass on the scans for P-L4-004's check. Exposure: I had read the step statement before this pass, so I knew its conclusion; but for seven of the twelve centres (f70v2, f72r3, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r, f73v) I had already recorded the centre earlier in this session as blind picture annotations (experiments PIC-<folio>/fleet-blue), before reading P-L4-004, and those records say the same thing. I did not use the transcription's words. Per centre, what stands inside the innermost disc, apart from the circular line of writing that bounds it, which I treat as running text: f70v2 (canvas 1006200): two fish, two stars; one short Voynich word next to the upper star, which has a tail line toward the upper fish; a word in the other, Latin-like script between the fish. The lower star has no word. f70v1 (1006201): a horned quadruped feeding at a green bush; the other-script word is written on its flank; no Voynich word. f71r (1006202): a horned quadruped at a green bush; other-script word on its body; no Voynich word (seen at reduced size only). f71v and f72r1 (1006203): each a bull-like quadruped at a green trough or bush, pale red and solid red; other-script word under the belly; no Voynich word. f72r2 (1006203): two clothed figures facing each other with joined hands; other-script word between them; no Voynich word. f72r3 (1006203): two clawed crustacean-like animals; other-script word under the lower one; no Voynich word. f72v3 and f72v2 (1006204): a clawed quadruped with a small plant, and a robed figure holding a star on a line; other-script word under or beside the emblem; the star in f72v2 has no word. f72v1 (1006205): a balance; other-script word below; no Voynich word. f73r (1006206): a quadruped with a looped tail under a large star; other-script word under its feet; the star has no word. f73v (1006207): a clothed figure with a crossbow; other-script word under the feet, close to the circular line; no Voynich word. So the nearest image object of the only standalone Voynich label is the upper star of f70v2, not the fish, and it has no drawn connection to the other-script word, from which the upper fish separates it. Three other centres contain a star (f72v2, f73r, and the lower star of f70v2) and none of those is labelled, so 'a labelled star in the centre' is the exception, not a pattern. I agree with P-L4-004: the centres give no picture-supported pairing of a Voynich word with a month word. I did not read or date the other-script words.
check: Open the canvases named and look inside each innermost disc; a single counter-example (a Voynich word inside a disc other than the one by the f70v2 upper star, and not part of the circular line) overturns this. The f71r centre should be re-checked at full resolution, since I saw it reduced.
